biography.plain_text: H. J. P. 'Jimmy' Bomford was a British businessman, motorboat racer and prominent collector of modern and ancient art. He won a leading outboard trophy in 1928 and assembled important holdings that included early Francis Bacon works. His enduring gifts to Swindon, Bristol and Oxford museums helped shape several public collections.

confidence.reason: DACS and the Contemporary Art Society identify the exact initials as a British local businessman, major donor and foundational figure for Swindon's collection. A period motorboating history documents the 1928 trophy, scholarly art history establishes his importance to early Francis Bacon collecting, and museum and family records document the wider Oxford and Bristol legacy.

long_biography.plain_text:
Bomford combined business with a lifelong appetite for boats and art. He raced hydroplanes in the 1920s and won the Duchess of York Trophy in Seahopper in 1928. He later competed in larger sailing vessels and acquired several large craft. His business interests ranged across the stock market, property and land ownership, although no single sector defines his surviving legacy.

By the 1940s, he had formed collections spanning modern British and European art, antiquities and ancient glass. A major wartime gift became the foundation of Swindon's modern collection. His patronage also gave the emigre artist Jankel Adler a home and studio. Later gifts and the Bomford Trust supported the Ashmolean and Bristol museums, leaving a legacy wider than any single collection.

review.notes: Terminal decision: H. J. P. 'Jimmy' Bomford is resolved at 97 identity confidence to the British businessman, motorboat racer and major collector Herbert James Powell Bomford (1896-1979). The collision-resistant bridge combines exact initials, nickname, dates, art provenance and period boating evidence; the unverified Sealion ownership is not relied upon. The identity card is 51 words and the independent two-paragraph profile is 121 words. United Kingdom residence, known-for title, male gender, birth year, death year and biography are proposed; day/month dates, birthplace and a full-name field replacement are withheld. All four wealth classifications remain Unknown because the principal wealth mechanism and starting platform are not established. Art collector is the sole approved active tag. Forbes and personal social searches were negative. Strict exact-input, active-tag and editorial validation passed without errors or warnings; nothing has been compiled or applied to the live system.
